about: Skill-routing dev set: 15 authored catalog skills x (2 positive + 1 negative). U-skill positives invoke the skill explicitly; U-skill negatives describe its task without invoking it. Stratified with holdout.json; tests/learn/trigger-prompts.test.ts holds the split and the leakage guard.

cases.prompt: Please run /ak:super-align on this before anyone writes code: I want some kind of team workspaces feature, but I honestly can't tell if it means shared billing, shared projects, or both.
Use the super-align skill with me. We keep arguing about whether notifications live per user or per org, and I want us to land somewhere I can sign off on.
I'm toying with adding offline mode to the mobile app but haven't decided what it should cover. What questions should we be asking first?
Please start /ak:super-bound on the audit logging direction we signed off yesterday (docs/direction/audit-log.md). Somebody new should be able to pick up each piece.
Invoke the super-bound skill for the search reindex work. We already said yes to the approach; I want the spec and the ticket graph.
Everyone agreed on how audit logging should work. Can you split it into a handful of tickets with acceptance criteria so I can hand them out?
Please run /ak:super-ship as a dry run on this branch; review and verification both passed this morning.
Use super-ship to get the retry backoff change ready to go out. It's been reviewed and checked.
This branch got approved and CI is green. Commit it, write up the PR description and push it.
Please run /ak:super-review in full mode on the payments refactor branch.
Use super-review to put the auth changes on this branch in front of a proper panel before I merge.
Can you look over the diff on this branch against the ticket and flag anything risky?
Please run /ak:compound: the flaky timezone test we just fixed taught us something about how fixtures pick up TZ, and I want it written down for next time.
Use the compound skill to record what we learned from today's migration rollback.
That took three hours because the cache key ignored the locale. Remember that so we don't hit it again.
Please run /ak:compound-refresh over our lessons; half of them mention the ORM we ripped out in March.
Use compound-refresh to go through the knowledgebase entries about deployment and sort out which still hold.
A lot of the notes we wrote down look stale since the rewrite. Go through them and clean up whichever are wrong now.
Please run /ak:receiving-review on PR 318; there are a dozen comments from the bot and two from Dana.
Use receiving-review to work through what people said on my open PR and tell me which comments hold up.
Reviewers left a bunch of comments on PR 318. Go through them and change whatever they asked for.
Please start /ak:babysit-pr on PR 412 while I'm stuck in meetings this afternoon.
Use babysit-pr for my PR: keep an eye on CI and comments and deal with whatever shows up.
Keep watching PR 412 and let me know when CI finishes.
Please run /ak:ultraqa against the signup flow now that the build is up on localhost:3000.
Use ultraqa on the CLI we just built; try to break it the way a nasty customer would.
The checkout page is deployed to staging. Poke at it like a malicious user and tell me what falls over.
Please run /ak:wayfind on how we get off the legacy monolith. It's months of work and nobody can see the route.
Use the wayfind skill for our multi-region effort; it's far too big to plan in one sitting.
We want to go multi-tenant eventually, but it's a huge murky project. How would you even start chipping at it?
Before we plan anything, find out how the config loader resolves its search paths and what we still don't know about it.
Map which modules touch the billing webhook and write down the evidence, no recommendations.
We have two config loaders in this codebase. Which one should we keep? I just want your call.
Ticket 42 is approved. Implement it test-first in its own worktree.
Pick up the approved ticket for the retry backoff and build it, red test first.
Quick one: fix the typo in the README heading, it says 'Instalation'.
Prove each acceptance criterion on this branch with the command you ran, its exit status and the commit.
The agent says the tests pass. Produce real evidence for every acceptance item instead.
Is src/parser.ts nicely structured? Give me your honest opinion of the code.
Review this ADR draft for contradictions and whether it is ready for a decision.
Read docs/plan.md and tell me where two of its sections disagree with each other.
Tighten the wording in docs/plan.md; it's clunky and runs too long.
The export job intermittently writes an empty file. Reproduce it and find the cause before touching code.
This test fails only on CI. Minimise it, form a hypothesis and fix it with a regression test.
I don't like how the logger prints timestamps. Switch it to ISO 8601.
